author: AntiTroll
quote:
I first played The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on the Nintendo 64 back in early 1999, and it immediately became my favourite game of all time. Ever since, I've dreamed of Nintendo giving OoT a full remake that could capture the magic of the original while bringing its world and presentation into the modern era. I've always imagined something along the lines of the incredible Zelda Wii U tech demo shown at E3 2011, and now that dream has finally become a reality.

The 2026 remake has exceeded my expectations in almost every conceivable way. I'm genuinely in awe of what Nintendo has accomplished here. From the breathtaking graphical presentation and art direction to the mesmerising sound design, performed by a full live orchestra, everything comes together to create an experience that feels both incredibly familiar and wonderfully revitalised.

Some of the boss fights were absolutely jaw-dropping. There were moments when I genuinely found myself just staring at the screen, taking in how beautiful everything looked. The environments, the atmosphere, the visual spectacle and the attention to detail are something else entirely.

What impressed me most is the care taken to expand upon certain areas, environments and moments throughout the original game. The additional cutscenes, environmental details and carefully modernised sections feel like natural extensions of the original vision rather than unnecessary additions. Nothing feels as though it has been changed simply for the sake of change. There's a genuine appreciation for what made Ocarina of Time so special in the first place, and that attention to detail is evident throughout the experience.

There is, however, one thing I don't think any conventional remake could ever fully recapture, and that's the sheer technological leap that Ocarina of Time represented when it first arrived on the Nintendo 64. Going from the relatively familiar 2D worlds of the Super Nintendo era to an expansive, fully realised 3D world that you could explore and interact with was something truly revolutionary. It wasn't simply an improvement in graphics. It fundamentally changed how we perceived, navigated and experienced video game worlds. That sense of discovery and technological wonder was a huge part of what made playing OoT for the first time so magical.

Replicating that particular feeling is practically impossible because we're no longer experiencing that same generational leap. In fact, the only way I could imagine Nintendo recreating something comparable would be through an entirely different approach to immersion, perhaps a panoramic augmented reality experience with VR functionality that could seamlessly transition into a first-person perspective. Obviously, that's a very different proposition from a traditional remake, but it illustrates just how groundbreaking the original experience was.

But perhaps the biggest surprise for me was what happened towards the end of the game. I honestly didn't think a remake could affect me emotionally in the same way the original did, but I was wrong. As the experience drew to a close, all those memories and emotions came rushing back so quickly that I actually found myself wiping away tears.

I went through a lot in my life around the time I first played Ocarina of Time in 1999, and here I am in 2026 going through some significant challenges all over again. It's difficult to explain, but in a strange way, Ocarina of Time has been there for me during some of the darkest periods of my life. It's always been somewhere I could escape to, somewhere I could leave the world behind for a little while and lose myself in an entirely different world and reality. Revisiting that world after all these years, experiencing it all over again in this way, brought back feelings I didn't even realise were still so close to the surface.

That's something I never expected this remake to achieve, and perhaps no review can really do justice to what that means to me.

I don't believe this should detract from what Nintendo has achieved. Judging the remake on its own merits, particularly its graphics, art direction, orchestral soundtrack, sound design, expanded storytelling, boss encounters and the way it has translated the original world into a modern experience, I honestly couldn't be happier.

Ocarina of Time was already my favourite game of all time, so I went into this remake with incredibly high expectations. Somehow, Nintendo has managed to meet them and, in many respects, surpass them.

**10/10.** An extraordinary remake of an extraordinary game. Just as magical as the original in its own right, and I genuinely never want to put the controller down again.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

quote: I cant get enough of this masterpeace, it easily holds its own as the best games ever made, I basically live and breath Days Gone, 10/10.

author: AntiTroll
quote: Days Gone is one of the most unfairly underrated masterpieces of all time, from the incredibly stunning, detailed & truly immersive open world, to the unbelievable attention to detail when it comes to constantly changing weather and shifting conditions of the terrain such as fog, rain, wind, mud and even dust to a mesmerizing night sky full of  stars, this game gets better and better the longer you play it. The story, dialogue and acting is top notch and the game has so much to do that you will continue to play it for weeks after you finish the main story. If I was given an option of only having the choice of a TLOU 3, a Resident Evil 9 and a Days Gone 3... I would have to choose Days Gone 3 its really just that special and I cant put into words how much of an underrated masterpiece this truly is 10/10.

author: AntiTroll
quote:
I had huge expectations of this game and I really wanted Nintendo to come through with the goods on this one and they did. The more I played Zelda BOTW the more and more I loved it, when making my way over mountains and across its gargantuan map I can't help but to stop and stare in awe at things like the sun setting, clouds rolling across the sky, the glow of the moonlight kissing the trees and each detailed blade of grass I pass,  the shimmer of the water or the stars in the sky and become completely mesmerised.
Pay no attention to the trolls who have crawled out from under their bridges to give review scores as low as 0 to try and discredit this masterpiece, regardless this game will go down in history as one of if not THE best game EVER MADE!!
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild
